scenario: AITA for keeping my son during my visitation instead of giving in to his mother? | I guess some backstory is due here. My ex and I have an 8 year old son, and we have been split up for a few years now. I have every other weekend parenting time along with a day during the week. It’s not enough time for me, but it’s what was legally decided through court. Her and I do not have the best relationship currently because I feel like I’m always being taken advantage of and I allow it because she always uses the “it’s for your son” excuse. I cherish my time with my son, but for the longest time, I allowed my ex to alter the parenting schedule to suit my son’s needs, whether for activities or family or if he just wasn’t feeling well. I always tried to be as accommodating as possible, even if it meant I didn’t see him for a week or more. Anyway, last Wednesday I was supposed to get him overnight, his mother called me and I asked if he could stay there since his cousin from out of town was staying with them. I reluctantly agreed but told her I wanted to get him Thursday instead. She agreed, and when Thursday came around, I texted her after work and said I was on my way to get him. She said they weren’t home, and I had to press her for information why. She decided to take the kids to a lake and said I needed to stop being grumpy because my son was having fun. We argued back and forth and since I did not drive all the way out to the lake to get him when I shouldn’t have had to in the first place, I told her that we should switch weekends (last weekend was hers, this one is mine) so that I had my make up time and his activities with her that fell on my weekend wouldn’t be interrupted. She refused, so now that my weekend is coming up, I’m not getting him at my regular time today because he’s at an amusement park with her family, and I am expected to give up even more of my valuable time tomorrow for their annual 4th of July party. Am I the asshole for putting my foot down and keeping my son during their family function so that I can enjoy time my son during my scheduled time?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm the asshole in this situation. Let me start by understanding the background. I'm an atheist, but I don't think that's directly related to the problem at hand. The main issue is about custody arrangements and how I handled a situation with my ex and our son. So, me and my ex have been split up for a few years. We have an 8-year-old son. The custody arrangement is every other weekend for me, plus a day during the week. I feel like this isn't enough time, but it's what the court decided. My ex and I don't have the best relationship. I feel like I'm always being taken advantage of, and I let it happen because she uses the "it's for the son" excuse. I do cherish the time I have with him, but I've been accommodating her a lot, even if it means not seeing him for a week or more. Last Wednesday, I was supposed to get him overnight. My ex called and asked if he could stay with her because her cousin was visiting. I reluctantly agreed but told her I wanted to get him on Thursday. She agreed. When Thursday came, I texted her after work to say I was on my way. She said they weren't home and I had to press her for info. She decided to take him to a lake and told me I needed to stop being grumpy because my son was having fun. We argued, and since I didn't want to drive all the way out to the lake, I told her we should switch weekends so I could make up the time and her activities on my weekend wouldn't be interrupted. She refused. Now, my weekend is coming up, and I'm not getting him at the regular time because he's at an amusement park with her family. I'm expected to give up even more of my time tomorrow for their annual 4th of July party. I put my foot down and kept my son during their family function so I can enjoy time with him during my scheduled time. Am I the asshole for this? Hmm, so I need to figure out if I'm being reasonable or if I'm overstepping. Let me break it down. First, the custody arrangement is legally decided, so I have every other weekend and a weekday. I've been accommodating her a lot, even when it means missing out on seeing my son. But in this case, she asked to keep him on Wednesday, and I agreed but wanted him back on Thursday. When Thursday came, she wasn't home and went to the lake instead. I didn't want to drive all the way, so I suggested switching weekends. She refused, and now I'm not getting him on my scheduled time because she's taking him to an amusement park and a party. I feel like I've been flexible, but she's not respecting the arrangement. By keeping him during her family functions, am I being unreasonable? Or is she not respecting the court order? I think the key points are: 1. The custody arrangement is legally binding. 2. I've been accommodating her, but she's not reciprocating. 3. She's using family activities as reasons to keep him, which are on my scheduled time. 4. I put my foot down, which led to her refusing to switch weekends. So, is it wrong for me to enforce the custody arrangement, or am I being too rigid? On one hand, the arrangement is there for a reason, and I have a right to see my son as per the court's decision. On the other hand, family activities are important, but they shouldn't override the legal custody schedule unless both parents agree. I also feel like I've been taken advantage of, and this time I stood my ground. Maybe I'm not the asshole because I'm just trying to enforce what's legally mine. But maybe I'm being too rigid and not considering the importance of family time for my son. Wait, but if I keep giving in, she might keep taking advantage. So, by setting boundaries, I'm protecting my rights and ensuring that my time with my son isn't constantly interrupted. However, by doing so, I might be missing out on some family activities, but those should be scheduled around the custody arrangement, not the other way around. I think the main issue is that she's not respecting the court order. If she wants to adjust the schedule, she should communicate that in advance, not just decide to keep him without discussing it. By refusing to switch weekends, she's making it difficult for me to have my scheduled time. So, in this case, I'm not the asshole. I'm just trying to enforce the custody arrangement that was legally decided. It's her responsibility to respect that and communicate any changes properly. By putting my foot down, I'm asserting my rights as a parent, which is reasonable.
